messages:
mira: Heads-up — customer 'AcmeRetail' on our Private VPC reported a regression after they applied a host kernel rollforward. Containers start, but GPU jobs fail with driver module mismatch. Seen on 3 nodes in their rack.

sam: Can you paste the exact error and a few quick checks (uname -r, nvidia-smi, lsmod)?

mira: Sure, pasted minimal logs (redacted):
```
uname -r: 5.15.0-1066-rt-amd64
$ nvidia-smi
NVIDIA-SMI has failed because it couldn't communicate with the NVIDIA driver. Make sure that the latest NVIDIA driver is installed and running.
$ dmesg | tail -n 10
[    4.123456] nvidia: module verification failed: signature and/or required key missing - tainting kernel
[    4.123457] nvidia: probe of 0000:01:00.0 failed with error -22
```

jordan: That -22 + "module verification" smells like a kernel ABI mismatch or missing signed module. On some customers we've seen custom RT/KVM kernels break DKMS-built nvidia modules.

alex: Are they on our supported driver matrix? Which driver/CUDA they pinned? Private deployments often drift because customers install vendor drivers themselves. We should confirm the customer wasn't applying a newer driver that requires CUDA 12+ kernels.

mira: They reported they didn't touch the driver; they only accepted a host kernel security update from their OS vendor. Their previous kernel was 5.15.0-1043. We suspect the nvidia module was compiled against the old kernel and DKMS didn't rebuild (or failed) after the kernel update.

sam: Two quick mitigations: 1) ask them to reboot into the previous kernel (if still present) to restore operations, 2) run dkms status and rebuild the module: `sudo dkms autoinstall` + `sudo modprobe nvidia`. But if they have Secure Boot enabled, unsigned modules will be blocked.

liz: If rebooting or DKMS rebuild isn't feasible, we can also fallback their routing to a hosted pool (temporary) — cost will spike but keeps customer live. Alternatives: enable their Dedicated pool to burst into our hosted region (requires infra policy change).

jordan: FYI we've seen a related NCCL error pattern earlier when module mismatches happen: `NCCL WARN Call to cudaGetDevice failed: invalid device ordinal` followed by hangs. So this aligns with what they're seeing in job logs.

alex: Action items I propose: (1) ask customer to run `uname -r && sudo dkms status && sudo modinfo nvidia` and paste output; (2) we should add a row to our supported matrix covering Ubuntu 22.04 derivatives with 5.15 RT kernels and documented Secure Boot behavior; (3) create a short KB for on-prem customers describing DKMS, Secure Boot, and kernel rollforward checks.

mira: I'm with (1)-(3). Also requesting engineering: can we add a preflight check in the redwood-agent to detect kernel-module ABI drift and surface a clear remediation? Right now it's just "nvidia not found" which customers misinterpret.

sam: We can add a healthprobe that runs at agent start: `modinfo nvidia || dkms status || kernel-abi-mismatch` and surface specific error codes. Low effort: a shell script + metrics. Medium effort: try automatic DKMS rebuild and report result (dangerous with signed modules). I'll open a ticket.

ops-bot: Scheduled window for emergency on-prem triage: 2025-03-28 02:00-04:00 UTC (tentative). Use incident channel if we need live warroom.

alex: Note on the matrix dispute: product & security disagreed earlier about officially supporting kernels with vendor patches. If we add those rows we need to coordinate SLA (we can't guarantee module rebuilds for arbitrary vendor kernels). Suggest we add "best-effort" label and required preflight checks.

jordan: Cost tradeoff: if we encourage customers to rely on our hosted fallback, that will increase cross-region egress and instance spend. We should price a "migration burst" for Private customers so support teams can propose it without surprise billing.

liz: I'll loop in CS to prep the customer messaging and payment ops for a billable temporary burst. CS: @acme-account-team please hold for an outbound with the mitigation options.

mira: Customer ran `dkms status` and attached output — it shows nvidia module not built for 5.15.0-1066. They have Secure Boot ON. They can either enroll a MOK and sign the module or roll back kernel. They prefer we avoid reboot if possible.

sam: For Secure Boot cases we shouldn't try auto-rebuild. Next steps: we provide clear steps (enroll MOK/signing guide) + ask them to schedule a maintenance window to boot old kernel if they prefer. Meanwhile we can enable temporary routing to hosted pool with explicit cost estimate.

alex: I'll prepare the supported-matrix PR to include a row for "Ubuntu 22.04 w/ RT/custom 5.15" with the note: Secure Boot => not supported unless modules are signed; DKMS auto-rebuild best-effort. Also adding test matrix to our CI for a kernel ABI check.

jordan: Quick engineering note — NCCL wheel/library compatibility checks should run at agent init as well. If cuda runtime not accessible, mark node as degraded and drain automatically.

mira: Great. I'll coordinate with the customer on the MOK instructions and their maintenance window. Also logging this as a customer driver-drift case for Private offering improvements.

sam: Ticket created: INFRA-1428 "agent preflight: kernel/module ABI checks + clear remediation". Assigning to eng-infra.

alex: PR for matrix & KB: will open by EOD.

mira: Thanks all — keep this thread for updates. :thumbsup:
